papers.title: Biofabrication of Cell‐Loaded 3D Spider Silk Constructs
papers.abstract: Biofabrication is an emerging and rapidly expanding field of research in which additive manufacturing techniques in combination with cell printing are exploited to generate hierarchical tissue-like structures. Materials that combine printability with cytocompatibility, so called bioinks, are currently the biggest bottleneck. Since recombinant spider silk proteins are non-immunogenic, cytocompatible, and exhibit physical crosslinking, their potential as a new bioink system was evaluated. Cell-loaded spider silk constructs can be printed by robotic dispensing without the need for crosslinking additives or thickeners for mechanical stabilization. Cells are able to adhere and proliferate with good viability over at least one week in such spider silk scaffolds. Introduction of a cell-binding motif to the spider silk protein further enables fine-tuned control over cell-material interactions. Spider silk hydrogels are thus a highly attractive novel bioink for biofabrication.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文探索了一种新的蜘蛛丝生物墨水用于3D生物打印，但完全未涉及任何人工智能或机器学习方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate any AI/ML technique into the bioprinting workflow, lacking intelligent control, optimization, or autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 寻找具有可打印性和细胞相容性的新型生物墨水
summary_zh.method: 使用重组蜘蛛丝蛋白作为生物墨水，通过机器人分配打印细胞负载结构
summary_zh.result: 蜘蛛丝水凝胶支持细胞粘附和增殖，无需交联添加剂
summary_zh.validation: 细胞活力检测和增殖实验验证材料相容性

summary_en.motivation: To develop a novel bioink that combines printability with cytocompatibility without the need for additives.
summary_en.method: Recombinant spider silk proteins were used as a bioink for robotic dispensing to fabricate cell-loaded 3D constructs.
summary_en.result: Spider silk hydrogels supported cell adherence and proliferation over a week without crosslinking additives.
summary_en.validation: Cell viability and proliferation assays confirmed cytocompatibility of the printed scaffolds.

papers.title: The association between comorbidities and pain, physical function and quality of life following hip and knee arthroplasty
papers.abstract: The aim of the study was to examine the relationship between comorbidities and pain, physical function and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA). A cross-sectional retrospective survey was conducted including 19 specific comorbidities, administered in patients who underwent THA or TKA in the previous 7-22 months in one of 4 hospitals. Outcome measures included pain, physical functioning, and HRQoL. Of the 521 patients (281 THA and 240 TKA) included, 449 (86 %) had ≥1 comorbidities. The most frequently reported comorbidities (>15 %) were severe back pain; neck/shoulder pain; elbow, wrist or hand pain; hypertension; incontinence of urine; hearing impairment; vision impairment; and cancer. Only the prevalence of cancer was significantly different between THA (n = 38; 14 %) and TKA (n = 52; 22 %) (p = 0.01). The associations between a higher number of comorbidities and worse outcomes were stronger in THA than in TKA. In multivariate analyses including all comorbidities with a prevalence of >5 %, in THA dizziness in combination with falling and severe back pain, and in TKA dizziness in combination with falling, vision impairments, and elbow, wrist or hand pain was associated with worse outcomes in most of the analyses. A broad range of specific comorbidities needs to be taken into account with the interpretation of patients' health status after THA and TKA. More research including the ascertainment of comorbidities preoperatively is needed, but it is conceivable that in particular, the presence of dizziness with falling, pain in other joints, and vision impairments should be assessed and treated in order to decrease the chance of an unfavorable outcome.

llm.relevance_to_user: 此论文为全髋/全膝关节置换术后合并症与患者报告结局的临床回顾性研究，未涉及任何生物力学建模、应力分析或微动计算。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not include any finite element analysis, stress shielding quantification, micromotion modeling, or implant design evaluation. It is purely a clinical outcomes study with patient-reported measures.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨合并症对全髋/膝关节置换术后疼痛、功能和生活质量的影响。
summary_zh.method: 回顾性横断面调查，纳入19种合并症，采用多变量分析。
summary_zh.result: 合并症数量与较差结局相关，THA中头晕伴跌倒和严重背痛影响最大。
summary_zh.validation: 基于521例患者数据的统计回归分析。

summary_en.motivation: To examine the relationship between specific comorbidities and patient-reported outcomes after total hip and knee arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A cross-sectional retrospective survey of 521 patients assessing the prevalence of 19 comorbidities and their association with pain, physical function, and health-related quality of life.
summary_en.result: A higher number of comorbidities was associated with worse outcomes, with dizziness combined with falling and severe back pain being most influential in THA.
summary_en.validation: Statistical multivariate regression analysis on patient-reported data from four hospitals.
